Graph neural network layers

Source: R/gnn-layers.R
gnn-layers.Rd

Layers are torch modules built on message_passing(). Every layer takes node features x (an N by F tensor, or list(x_src, x_dst) for bipartite relations where noted) and a one based long edge_index (2 by E, row 1 source, row 2 target), and returns one row per target node. Messages flow from source to target, so a node aggregates over its incoming edges. For undirected graphs, graph_data() stores both directions, so this is the usual neighborhood.

Usage

sage_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  aggr = "mean",
  root_weight = TRUE,
  normalize = FALSE,
  bias = TRUE
)

gcn_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  add_self_loops = TRUE,
  normalize = TRUE,
  improved = FALSE,
  bias = TRUE
)

graph_conv(in_features, out_features, aggr = "sum", bias = TRUE)

gin_conv(nn, eps = 0, train_eps = FALSE, edge_dim = NULL, in_features = NULL)

gat_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  heads = 1L,
  concat = TRUE,
  negative_slope = 0.2,
  dropout = 0,
  add_self_loops = TRUE,
  edge_dim = NULL,
  bias = TRUE
)

gatv2_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  heads = 1L,
  concat = TRUE,
  negative_slope = 0.2,
  dropout = 0,
  add_self_loops = TRUE,
  edge_dim = NULL,
  bias = TRUE
)

transformer_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  heads = 1L,
  concat = TRUE,
  dropout = 0,
  edge_dim = NULL,
  root_weight = TRUE,
  bias = TRUE
)

nn_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  edge_dim = NULL,
  edge_nn = NULL,
  aggr = "sum",
  root_weight = TRUE,
  bias = TRUE
)

rgcn_conv(
  in_features,
  out_features,
  num_relations,
  num_bases = NULL,
  aggr = "mean",
  root_weight = TRUE,
  bias = TRUE
)

Arguments

in_features

Input feature size. sage_conv, graph_conv, gat_conv, gatv2_conv and transformer_conv also accept c(source, target) sizes for bipartite input.

out_features

Output feature size (per head for attention layers).

aggr

Aggregation, see scatter_aggregate().

root_weight

Add a transformed copy of the target node's own features.

normalize

For sage_conv, L2 normalize the output rows; for gcn_conv, apply the symmetric degree normalization.

bias

Learn an additive bias.

add_self_loops

Add self loops before propagation.

improved

Self loop weight 2 instead of 1 (gcn_conv).

nn

A module applied after aggregation (gin_conv), for example an MLP from graph_mlp(). For gin_conv its input size must equal the node feature size.

eps

Initial \(\epsilon\).

train_eps

Learn \(\epsilon\).

edge_dim

Edge feature size. For gin_conv this turns on the GINE variant, \(\sum_j \mathrm{ReLU}(x_j + W_e e_{ji})\); for attention layers edge features enter the attention scores.

heads

Number of attention heads.

concat

Concatenate heads (output size heads * out_features); otherwise average them.

negative_slope

Slope of the LeakyReLU in the attention score.

dropout

Dropout probability on attention coefficients (training only).

edge_nn

Module mapping edge features (E by edge_dim) to E by in_features * out_features (nn_conv). When NULL, a two layer MLP with 32 hidden units is built from edge_dim.

num_relations

Number of relation types; edge_type holds codes 1:num_relations.

num_bases

Use basis decomposition with this many bases (NULL for a full weight per relation).

Value

An nn_module.

Details

LayerUpdate for node \(i\)Edge inputSelf loops
sage_conv\(W_1 \mathrm{aggr}_{j} w_{ji} x_j + W_2 x_i\)edge_weightnone added
gcn_conv\(\sum_j \frac{w_{ji}}{\sqrt{d_j d_i}} W x_j + b\)edge_weightadded to nodes without one
graph_conv\(W_1 \sum_j w_{ji} x_j + W_2 x_i\)edge_weightnone added
gin_conv\(\mathrm{MLP}((1+\epsilon) x_i + \sum_j x_j)\)edge_attr (GINE), edge_weightnone added
gat_conv\(\sum_j \alpha_{ij} W x_j\), \(\alpha\) from \(a^\top [W x_i \Vert W x_j]\)edge_attrreplaced: existing removed, one per node added
gatv2_conv\(\sum_j \alpha_{ij} W_s x_j\), \(\alpha\) from \(a^\top \mathrm{LeakyReLU}(W_s x_j + W_t x_i)\)edge_attras gat_conv
transformer_conv\(W_r x_i + \sum_j \alpha_{ij} (W_v x_j + W_e e_{ji})\)edge_attrnone added
nn_conv\(W x_i + \mathrm{aggr}_j x_j \Theta(e_{ji})\)edge_attr (required)none added
rgcn_conv\(W_0 x_i + \sum_r \frac{1}{|N_r(i)|}\sum_{j \in N_r(i)} W_r x_j\)edge_type (required)none added

Cost is \(O(E F)\) for message construction plus the dense transforms (\(O(N F F')\)); attention layers keep an E by heads attention tensor; nn_conv stores an E by F by F' tensor of edge specific weights and is the most memory hungry. All layers are permutation equivariant: permuting node rows and relabeling edge_index permutes the output rows the same way.

The formulas follow the PyTorch Geometric layers of the same names (SAGEConv, GCNConv, GraphConv, GINConv/GINEConv, GATConv, GATv2Conv, TransformerConv, NNConv, RGCNConv) for the options exposed here; options not listed are not implemented.

Attention layers keep the coefficients of their last forward pass in layer$last_attention (a list with edge_index and an E by heads tensor alpha). Attention coefficients describe how the model weighted neighbors; they are not by themselves measures of feature importance or causal relevance.

References

Hamilton, Ying and Leskovec (2017) Inductive representation learning on large graphs. Kipf and Welling (2017) Semi-supervised classification with graph convolutional networks. Xu et al. (2019) How powerful are graph neural networks? Velickovic et al. (2018) Graph attention networks. Brody, Alon and Yahav (2022) How attentive are graph attention networks? Shi et al. (2021) Masked label prediction. Gilmer et al. (2017) Neural message passing for quantum chemistry. Schlichtkrull et al. (2018) Modeling relational data with graph convolutional networks. Morris et al. (2019) Weisfeiler and Leman go neural.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  x <- torch::torch_randn(4, 3)
  ei <- torch::torch_tensor(rbind(c(1L, 2L, 3L), c(2L, 3L, 4L)),
                            dtype = torch::torch_long())
  layer <- sage_conv(3, 5)
  layer(x, ei)$shape
  gat_conv(3, 2, heads = 2)(x, ei)$shape
}
#> [1] 4 4
